compare.intro: This unit's look-alikes split like this: こそ picks out the one that matters, さえ an extreme case, and まで one more thing on top; a noun + ばかり is too much of one thing, te-form + ばかりいる is doing one thing over and over, and ばかりでなく, like だけでなく, adds a second thing, usually with も; なんて can follow a whole clause or quoted words to show surprise or make light of them, while など (playing down) mostly sits after a noun; and くらい asks for at least a small thing, でも offers a loose example, and さえ points to an extreme case.

forms.tag: 極端な例 · even (the extreme case)
forms.ja: この[道|みち]は暗くて、昼で{さえ}少し[怖|こわ]いです。
forms.en: This road is so dark that it is a little scary even in the daytime.

forms.tag: そのうえ · even this, on top
forms.ja: [宿題|しゅくだい]を[忘|わす]れて、[教科書|きょうかしょ]{まで}家に[置|お]いてきてしまいました。
forms.en: I forgot my homework, and even left my textbook at home.

forms.tag: せめて · at least (a small thing)
forms.ja: [忙|いそが]しくても、[返事|へんじ]{くらい}できるでしょう。
forms.en: Even if you are busy, you can at least reply.

check.label: Just one small thing
check.q: ^ほかのことはしなくていいから^、花に水（　　）やっておいてね。
why: まで adds one more thing on top of others. ほかのことはしなくていい says there is nothing else to add to.
Nothing else is needed, so ask for just this one small thing: 水くらい.
さえ points to an extreme case. To mean "just this", it needs a condition with ば, as in 水さえやってくれればいい.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: 林さんは^[会議|かいぎ]の間ずっと^[窓|まど]の外を（　　）、話を聞いていませんでした。
why: The ta-form + ばかり means "have just done". It clashes with [会議|かいぎ]の間ずっと, the whole meeting.
ばかりでなく adds a second fact of the same kind, usually with も. Here not listening is what came of looking outside, and there is no も.
The te-form + ばかりいる: one thing the whole time, and a complaint follows.
なんて would show surprise at looking outside, but no reaction follows. The sentence goes straight on to what he did not do.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: 十年も[続|つづ]いたあの[番組|ばんぐみ]が終わる（　　）、^ちょっとさびしいですね^。
why: なんて follows a whole clause in the plain form and shows a feeling about it, here a little sadness.
In everyday speech, など does not follow a whole clause like this to show a feeling. Playing-down など sits after a noun, as in わたしなど.
ばかり does not introduce a reaction to news. 終わるばかり cannot be followed by ちょっとさびしいですね.
さえ marks an extreme example. It does not follow the dictionary form of a verb like 終わる.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: [面接|めんせつ]できんちょうして、^[簡単|かんたん]な[質問|しつもん]^（　　）答えられませんでした。
why: くらい plays a thing down in a request or a complaint, as in これくらいできるでしょう. It does not report what you were unable to do.
でも would offer a loose example, "an easy question or something", which makes no sense with 答えられませんでした.
こそ picks out the one that matters most. Easy questions are not the point here; they are the extreme case.
Even the easy questions, the extreme case, were too much. に stays in front of さえ.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: この[祭|まつ]りはにぎやか（　　）、^食べ物も^おいしいです。
why: A な-adjective needs な before ばかり. Even にぎやかなばかりで would mean "only lively", which clashes with the good food added with も.
Not only lively, the food is good too: keep な before ばかりでなく, and the second point takes も.
ばかりいる follows the te-form of a verb, for an action done again and again. にぎやか is a state, not an action.
こそ follows a noun and picks out the one that matters. It cannot follow にぎやか, and this sentence adds a second good point with も.

drill.label: Build the sentence
drill.before: 兄は試験の前の日なのに、
drill.hint: ばかりいて follows a te-form. What does he do all the time, and what has he not even opened?
drill.full: 兄は試験の前の日なのに、ギターをひいて{ばかりいて}[教科書|きょうかしょ]さえ開いていません。
drill.explain: ギターを, ひいて, ばかりいて, [教科書|きょうかしょ]. ギターをひいてばかりいて says he does nothing but play the guitar. [教科書|きょうかしょ] goes right before さえ: he has not even opened his textbook, the extreme case.

drill.label: Build the sentence
drill.before: この作家の本は、日本の
drill.hint: ばかりでなく follows the first group of readers. Which group is the surprising extra?
drill.full: この作家の本は、日本の読者{ばかりでなく}海外の人にまで読まれています。
drill.explain: 読者, ばかりでなく, 海外の人, にまで. 日本の読者ばかりでなく is the first group; 海外の人にまで adds a surprising second one. に marks who reads the books (読まれています) and stays in front of まで.

exam.label: Choose the form
exam.q: 駅前にできた新しいビルは、まだ空いている部屋（　　）だそうだ。
exam.explain: Noun + ばかり: almost all the rooms are still empty. ばかりでなく needs a second thing after it, not だ. こそ picks out one thing as the one that matters, and さえ marks an extreme case; neither makes sense right before だ here.

exam.label: Choose the form
exam.q: 疲れた（　　）言っていないで、早く手伝って。
exam.explain: なんて can follow quoted words like 疲れた and makes light of them: stop saying things like that. など would need と here (疲れたなどと). こそ and さえ cannot follow quoted words like this.

exam.label: Build the sentence
exam.after: 最後に夢をかなえられるのだと思う。
exam.full: あきらめずに勉強を{続けた}人こそ最後に夢をかなえられるのだと思う。
exam.explain: 勉強を, 続けた, 人, こそ. 勉強を続けた describes 人, and こそ follows 人 to say these are the people who, above all, reach their dream.

scene.en: The patient guide board at a hospital
scene.intro: Tap each word on the board that a patient needs on the way to see the doctor and back.

check.label: How the exam asks it
check.q: 初めての方は、_保険証_を受付に出してください。
check.explain: 保険証 is ほけんしょう: 保 ホ, short (not ほう), 険 ケン, not voiced (not げん), and 証 ショウ, long (not しょ).

skill.ask: Which rules on the notice apply to Tamura's visit, and what does Tamura have to do?
skill.passage:
みなみ病院　面会のご案内
①面会時間は、平日は午後2時から午後8時まで、^土曜・日曜・祝日は午前11時から午後8時まで^です。
②面会の方は、^まず1階の面会窓口で^名前と病室の番号を書いて、^面会カードを受け取ってください^。
③一度に面会できるのは、3人までです。
④^小学生以下のお子さんは、病室に入れません^。^3階のラウンジで会ってください^。
⑤^病院の中に花を持ちこむことはできません^。
⑥熱やせきがある方は、面会をお休みください。
skill.strategy: Find the day and time of the visit first, then check who is coming and what Tamura wants to bring.

item.q: 田村さんは、11月8日（日）の午後1時に、5歳の娘といっしょに、入院している母に会いに行きます。母のために花を買っていくつもりです。田村さんはどうすればいいですか。
options: 面会カードを受け取って、娘と病室で母に会う。花は持っていかない。
面会カードを受け取って、花を持って、娘と3階のラウンジで母に会う。
花は買わずに行き、面会カードを受け取って、娘と3階のラウンジで母に会う。
午後1時は面会時間ではないので、別の日に娘と行く。
short: 花を持ってラウンジで
item.explain: Rule ① puts Sunday visits from 11:00, so 1 p.m. is fine. Rule ② says to get a visitor card first, rule ④ sends a five-year-old to the 3rd-floor lounge, and rule ⑤ bans flowers anywhere in the hospital.
why: Tamura's daughter is five, so she cannot go into the ward room (rule ④).
No flowers may be brought into the hospital at all, the lounge included (rule ⑤).
11月8日 is a Sunday, and on Sundays visits start at 11:00, so 1 p.m. is within the hours (rule ①).
